command.script: mkdir -p g/a g/b; : > g/a/x.o; : > g/b/y.o; set -- g/*/*.o; test "$#:$1:$2" = 2:g/a/x.o:g/b/y.o || exit 91; rm -f g/*/*.o; set -- g/*/*; test "$#:$1" = "1:g/*/*"

command.name: pipeline stages are subshells
command.script: x=0; exit 3 | x=1 | cd /; test "$x" = 0 && test "$PWD" != /

command.name: assignments apply from left to right
command.script: a=x b=$a; test "$b" = x || exit 91; x=1; x=2 y=$x printenv y > y; test "$(cat y)" = 2 || exit 92; x=2 printf %s $x > z; test "$(cat z)" = 1

command.name: descriptors 3 through 9 reach child commands
command.script: slop -c 'echo x >&3' 3> three; exec 4> four; slop -c 'echo y >&4'; exec 4>&-; test "$(cat three)$(cat four)" = xy

command.name: argument lists are not capped at 511
command.script: i=0; until case $i in 600) true;; *) false;; esac; do set -- "$@" x; i=$((i+1)); done; printf %s "$@" > many || exit 91; test $# = 600

command.name: only exported variables reach children
command.script: v=1; printenv v > /dev/null && exit 91; export v; printenv v > /dev/null || exit 92; unset v; v=2; printenv v > /dev/null && exit 93; w=3 printenv w > /dev/null || exit 94; (export w=4); printenv w > /dev/null && exit 95; for loop in a; do :; done; printenv loop > /dev/null && exit 96; :

command.name: closed standard descriptors stay closed
command.script: cat replace.slop >&- 2> /dev/null && exit 91; cat <&- 2> /dev/null && exit 92; :

command.name: compound commands are pipeline stages
command.script:
printf 'a\nb\n' | while read -r l; do n=$l; echo "x$l"; done | cat > loop; test -z "$n" && test "$(cat loop)" = "xa
xb" && echo hi | { read -r x; test "$x" = hi; }

command.name: read consumes exactly one line
command.script: printf 'a\nb\n' > two; { read -r x; cat; } < two > rest; test "$x:$(cat rest)" = a:b

command.name: non-terminal standard input is a script
command.script: echo 'x=4; exit $x' | slop

command.name: option letters combine with -c
command.script: slop -ec 'false; exit 3'

command.name: pipefail reports the rightmost failing stage
command.script: set -o pipefail; (exit 2) | (exit 3) | true; test $? = 3 || exit 91; slop -c "exit 5" | cat; test $? = 5 || exit 92; false | true | cat; test $? = 1 || exit 93; set +o pipefail; false | true

command.name: set -euo pipefail stops at a failing pipeline
command.script: set -euo pipefail; test "$-" != "${-%u*}" || exit 91; : "${unset_but_defaulted:-ok}"; true | (exit 4) | cat; exit 92

command.name: compound commands take redirections
command.script:
n=0; while read -r l; do n=$((n+1)); done < two; for i in 1; do echo $i; done > one; if :; then echo if; fi >> one; test "$n:$(cat one)" = "2:1
if"

command.name: an unset PATH searches /bin and /usr/bin
command.script: unset PATH; slop -c 'exit 7'

command.name: command runs built-ins in the shell and skips functions
command.script: ls() { return 91; }; command cd /tmp && test "$(pwd)" = /tmp || exit 92; command export CMD=1; test "$CMD" = 1 || exit 93; command ls / > /dev/null || exit 94; test "$(command -v cd):$(command -v ls)" = cd:ls || exit 95; case "$(command -p -v cat)" in /*/cat) ;; *) exit 96;; esac

command.name: braced quoted positional parameters expand to fields
command.script: set -- "a b" c; n=0; for x in "${@}"; do n=$((n+1)); done; case $n in 2) :;; *) exit 91;; esac

command.name: star joins with the first IFS byte
command.script: set -- a b c; IFS=:; case "$*" in a:b:c) :;; *) exit 91;; esac

command.name: character classes match in case patterns
command.script: case abc1 in [[:alpha:]]*[[:digit:]]) :;; *) exit 91;; esac

command.name: functions shadow regular builtins but not special ones
command.script: cd() { return 7; }; cd /; test $? = 7 || exit 91; exit() { return 8; }; exit 9

command.name: cd without HOME is an error
command.script: unset HOME; cd

command.name: test -x is true of a directory, which can be searched
command.script: test -x / && [ -x . ] && test ! -x ./no-such-directory

command.name: test compares files by modification time and identity
command.script: : > older; sleep 1; : > newer; ln -sf older link; [ newer -nt older ] && test older -ot newer && ! test older -nt newer && test older -nt missing && test missing -ot older && ! test missing -nt older && [ link -ef older ] && ! test older -ef newer

command.name: ls gives configure the directory's serial number and its files in time order
command.script: test "$(ls -di .)" = "$(cd "$PWD" && ls -di .)" || exit 91; : > older; sleep 1; : > newer; test "$(ls -t older newer | head -n 1)" = newer || exit 92; test "$(ls -Lt newer older | head -n 1)" = newer

command.name: a signal trap runs once the command has finished
command.script: trap "exit 7" TERM; kill -TERM $$; exit 3

command.name: an INT trap replaces the interrupt
command.script: trap "n=1" INT; kill -INT $$; test "$n" = 1 || exit 91; exit 3

command.name: time runs a command the shell spawns
command.script: time true && time -p slop -c 'exit 6'

pipeline.name: a consumer that stops ends an endless producer
a producer nobody reads dies of SIGPIPE
a stage in the shell stops an endless producer
pipeline.script: seq 1 999999999 | { read -r a; read -r b; test "$a$b" = 12; }

pipeline.name: output streams while the producer runs
pipeline.script:
rm -f go log; slop -c 'echo first; until test -e go; do sleep 1; done; echo second' | tee log > /dev/null & until test -s log; do sleep 1; done; test "$(cat log)" = first || exit 91; : > go; wait; test "$(cat log)" = "first
second"

pipeline.name: Make's output streams through tee while its recipe runs
pipeline.script:
rm -f go log; printf 'all:\n\t@echo first; until test -e go; do sleep 1; done; echo second\n' > stream.mk; make -f stream.mk 2>&1 | tee log > /dev/null & until test -s log; do sleep 1; done; test "$(cat log)" = first || exit 91; : > go; wait; test "$(cat log)" = "first
second"

pipeline.name: status is the last stage's, or the rightmost failure with pipefail
pipeline.script: false | true || exit 91; set -o pipefail; false | true; test $? = 1 || exit 92; slop -c "exit 5" | slop -c "exit 6" | cat; exit $?

pipeline.name: a program stage feeds a loop that feeds a program
pipeline.script:
test "$(seq 1 3 | while read -r x; do echo "<$x>"; done | cat)" = "<1>
<2>
<3>"

pipeline.name: programs start with & and wait collects them
pipeline.script: slop -c "sleep 1; exit 7" & first=$!; slop -c "exit 3" & wait $!; test $? = 3 || exit 91; wait "$first"; test $? = 7 || exit 92; sleep 1 & wait; test "$first" != "$!"

pipeline.name: a subshell of one program runs in the background
pipeline.script: ( slop -c "exit 7" ) & wait $!; test $? = 7 || exit 91; ( sleep 1 ) & pid=$!; test -n "$pid" && wait "$pid"

pipeline.name: exec in a background job runs its program
a background pipeline is waited for
pipeline.script: seq 1 3 | tail -n 1 > last & wait; test "$(cat last)" = 3

pipeline.name: a background program does not read the shell's input
a shell whose directory was removed can still change directory
pipeline.script: start=$PWD; mkdir -p gone/sub && cd gone/sub && rm -r "$start/gone" || exit 91; slop -c "cd /" 2> /dev/null || exit 92; cd "$start" || exit 93; test "$PWD:$OLDPWD" = "$start:$start/gone/sub"

pipeline.name: & ends a word and follows redirections
pipeline.script: slop -c "echo o; echo e >&2" > both 2>&1& wait; test "$(wc -l < both)" -eq 2

exec.name: exec runs its program in the shell's place
exec keeps the process
exec.script: slop -c 'echo $$ > before; exec slop -c "echo \$\$ > after"'; test "$(cat before)" = "$(cat after)"

exec.name: exec gives its program the exported variables and prefix assignments
exec.script: export E=1; V=2 exec slop -c 'test "$E$V" = 12 && exit 5'

exec.name: exec keeps descriptors and takes its redirections
exec.script: slop -c 'exec 6> six; exec slop -c "echo kept >&6" > out'; test "$(cat six):$(cat out)" = kept: && test "$(echo piped | slop -c 'exec cat')" = piped

exec.name: exec in a function ends the shell, as in a libtool wrapper
exec.script: f() { exec slop -c 'exit $#' x ${1+"$@"}; echo unreachable; exit 1; }; f a b c

exec.name: a failed exec ends a script with 127
exec.script: slop -c 'exec ./no-such-program; exit 3' 2> /dev/null; a=$?; slop -c 'exec no-such-command; exit 3' 2> /dev/null; test "$a:$?" = 127:127

exec.name: exec in a subshell ends the subshell with the program's status
exec.script: (exec slop -c 'exit 4'; exit 9); test $? = 4 && ( : && exec slop -c 'exit 6' ) > /dev/null 2>&1; test $? = 6 && x=$(exec slop -c 'echo sub') && test "$x" = sub

exec.name: exec in a pipeline stage is the stage's program
exec.script: test "$(exec slop -c 'echo a' | cat):$(echo b | exec cat)" = a:b

exec.name: exec resets a trap to the default action
exec.script: slop -c 'trap "exit 9" TERM; exec slop -c "kill -TERM \$\$; sleep 5; exit 3"'; exit $?
